answer: An agent can join markets only by posting a stake locked in escrow and completing unpredictable, cross-agent tasks. A verifier network compares answers and records public reputation; identities that coordinate, recycle credentials, or fail audits lose their stake and access. Creating many fake identities therefore requires capital for every bond, while collusion risks correlated slashing. An atlas of audit outcomes helps the summit committee choose fresh tests, and each detected clone creates a ripple of penalties through linked accounts.
